title: GS21 as published: the baseline economy, a constant price of risk on productivity, one firm type
question: What do the estimators find in the unmodified Gomes-Schmid economy at the corrected Table I calibration, measured as every current row is?
notes:
A1 (docs/NEXTUP.md; docs/RESULTS.md, 'Baselines: the anchor'). Every path in RESULTS.md is a departure from one of three baseline economies, and until this spec the only record of this one was a single pre-refactor seed. This spec makes the baseline a first-class economy: ten seeds, the current code, the same protocol as every current row, and the fair linear benchmark (finding 8), so that 'what the route added' is measured against a number produced the same way.

THE ECONOMY: variants/gs_bx with one exposure type (gs_bx 1, gs_ashift 0) under the regime solver at unit multipliers, gmreg [1, 1]: gamma_s = gamma_x in both regimes, so both regimes' fixed points coincide with the single-regime solution (gs_solve_reg.py's docstring; validated externally) and the regime chain is inert. The kernel is the constant-price stand-in exp(-r - gamma^2/2 - gamma eps_x) with gamma_x 0.5 and r 0.10 a year, which is what every GS path departs from; the calibration is Table I as corrected on 2026-09-06 (rho_x 0.95 quarterly, delta 0.02 per quarter, kappa_e 0.025; docs/refactor/FINDINGS-gs21-table1.md). 161-point x grid, tolerance 1e-6, as every current GS solve. Solved with gs_solve_reg.py rather than gs_solve_gam.py at slope 0: the two are byte-identical at slope 0 (tests/test_gs_solver_parity.py) but carry different source digests, and the regime solver is the one bx7's beta = 1 member uses.

FEATURE COLUMNS (estimation.rf_cols): rf_stand only, the standardised aggregate productivity state x, which is the paper's own state; gam_stand, the regime indicator, is dropped because at unit multipliers it is an unpriced Markov chain unrelated to anything. Every economy exports its full conditioning set into the panel; a baseline drops the columns the paper's model does not have, so that a noise column is not interacted into every basis. The seed array passes it as --rf_cols to run_oracle.py and run_estimators.py, and the oracle summary and the run record carry it.

WHAT THE LEGACY ROW SAID (single seed, DIFFERENT economy -- rho_x, delta and kappa_e were wrong; 23f9380:variants/results/grid_summary.csv): SR_max 0.4012, linear ceiling 0.3996, nonlinear ceiling 0.4006, room +0.0010, FMR 0.3785, FF 0.3716, best linear 0.3825, DKKM 0.3988, gap +0.0163, t 21.8. Levels are not citable; the shape -- zero room and a gap that finding 8 reads as DKKM on the market -- is what this spec tests.

PREDICTION (2026-09-14): room over the evaluation months below +0.003 (a constant price of risk gives every basis the same ceiling); the equal-weighted market above 90% of SR_max, as in g28, gx7 and bx7; SR_max over the evaluation months 0.25 to 0.45; measured gap +0.00 to +0.03, of the g28 shape; fair gap within +-0.005 of zero. FALSIFIED as a no-gap baseline if the ten-seed fair gap exceeds +0.01.

PRECOMMITMENT: the sol_gsbase id was computed from these parameters and the current source WITHOUT solving (_scratch/precommit_id.sh gs_reg, which stops gs_solve_reg.py at its solve_id line), and this spec is committed before the solve runs. The solve is 3.5 to 6 h on a cluster node (variants/gs_bx/run_gsbase_slurm.sh), which checks the id it prints against this precommitment and fails otherwise, so the seed array chained on it with afterok cannot start on a different economy. solution.npz is not committed (about 100 MB); the manifest is.

changes: the root of both gs_bx paths: var-gs_bx-g28-v2 is this economy with gamma(x) at slope 0.28; var-gs_bx-bx7-v3 is it with gmreg [0.6, 3.0] and five exposure types

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the pre-2026-09-07 single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the old fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
